title: Life Science — The Miracle of Living Things
description: Test your understanding of cells, classification, plants, animals, the human body, and ecosystems.

questions.question: What is the basic unit of life?
options: An atom
A cell
A tissue
A molecule
questions.explanation: The cell is the basic unit of life. All living things are made of one or more cells, and a cell is the smallest structure that can carry out all the functions of a living organism.

questions.question: Which organelle is responsible for photosynthesis in plant cells?
options: Mitochondria
Nucleus
Chloroplast
Cell membrane
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts are organelles found in plant cells that contain chlorophyll and capture sunlight to convert carbon dioxide and water into glucose and oxygen through photosynthesis.

questions.question: Who developed the modern system of biological classification and is known as the 'Father of Taxonomy'?
options: Charles Darwin
Robert Hooke
Carl Linnaeus
Louis Pasteur
questions.explanation: Carl Linnaeus, a devout Christian scientist, developed the hierarchical classification system and binomial nomenclature that is still used today. He saw classifying organisms as a way of understanding God's design in creation.

questions.question: According to Genesis 1, God created living things 'according to their kinds.' What does this mean for how we understand the diversity of life?
options: All organisms descended from a single common ancestor
God created distinct groups of organisms, and while variation occurs within kinds, one kind does not change into a fundamentally different kind
No variation is possible within any group of organisms
All organisms were created looking exactly as they do today with no variation
questions.explanation: The Biblical concept of 'created kinds' teaches that God made distinct groups of organisms. Significant variation can occur within a kind (such as the many breeds of dogs), but one kind does not transform into an entirely different kind.

questions.question: What is homeostasis?
options: The process by which plants make food from sunlight
The body's ability to maintain a stable internal environment despite changing external conditions
The classification of organisms into kingdoms
The flow of energy through a food chain
questions.explanation: Homeostasis is the body's ability to maintain a stable internal environment — such as body temperature, blood sugar levels, and pH balance — despite constantly changing external conditions. This self-regulating ability reflects God's remarkable design.

questions.question: In a food chain, what role do producers play?
options: They hunt and eat other animals
They break down dead organisms and return nutrients to the soil
They convert sunlight into energy through photosynthesis, forming the base of the food chain
They regulate the population of predators
questions.explanation: Producers, mainly plants, convert sunlight into energy through photosynthesis. They form the base of every food chain, providing the energy that sustains all other organisms in the ecosystem.

questions.question: Why does the third principle of cell theory — that all cells come from pre-existing cells — support the Biblical view of creation?
options: Because it proves evolution is true
Because scientists have observed life arising from non-living matter many times
Because it shows that life cannot arise spontaneously from non-living matter, pointing to an original Creator who made the first living cells
Because cells can create themselves from simple chemicals
questions.explanation: Since all cells come from pre-existing cells and life has never been observed arising from non-living matter, there must have been an original Creator who made the first living cells. This is consistent with the Biblical account of God creating life directly.

questions.question: According to Genesis 2:15, what responsibility did God give humans regarding His creation?
options: To exploit all natural resources without concern
To worship nature as divine
To work it and take care of it — to be faithful stewards
To leave nature completely untouched
questions.explanation: God placed humans in the Garden to 'work it and take care of it,' establishing our role as stewards of His creation. We are to use natural resources wisely while caring for the environment God entrusted to us.
